caption: The pre-tirzepatide portfolio, product by product: Trulicity ~49% of US injectable GLP-1 prescriptions, Jardiance 60% of SGLT2, Taltz 19% of IL-17 dermatology, Emgality 37% TRx. The share baseline the incretin era is measured against.

Medicines launched since 2014 reached nearly 60% of core revenue by 2021 - the payoff from the 2014-2020 launch wave (Trulicity, Jardiance, Taltz, Verzenio, Emgality) before tirzepatide existed as a product.

The fixed/variable cost split, disclosed once and never since: 53% fixed / 47% variable in 2016 moving to 47% / 53% by 2020. A majority-variable cost base is why 50% volume growth against a 6% price decline still expands margin.
Non-GAAP operating margin excluding Elanco: 20.7% (2016) to ~30% (2021 guidance), over 900bp of expansion. The starting point for a margin path that reached 45.0% reported in Q1 2026.

2017-2021 capital allocation, human pharma only: $22.6bn after-tax R&D, $14.0bn business development, only $5.5bn capital investments, ~70% growth / ~30% return. Business development ran 2.5x capex - the inverse of FY2025.
Total shareholder return January 2017 to December 2021: Lilly 270%, Novo Nordisk 233%, peer average 68%. Management's own framing of the pre-incretin decade, on the proxy peer group.

The decade-long financial frame, and the commitment that broke: mid-single-digit annual net price declines on average, ~80% gross margin maintained, SG&A as the operating-margin lever, limited patent exposure in the next five years.

The R&D productivity claim in its original form: 16 new medicines delivered in 8 years (2014-2021) against a 20-in-10 target, with tirzepatide, donanemab and pirtobrutinib flagged as ~$3bn+ consensus peak-sales launches for 2022-23.

The genetic-medicines platform build, bought modality by modality - Dicerna siRNA (2018), Precision gene editing and Prevail gene therapy (2020), MiNA saRNA and ProQR mRNA editing (2021) - reaching >20% of the diabetes, immunology and neuroscience research portfolio.

The obesity opportunity as management sized it in December 2021: over 100 million people with obesity in the US, less than 3% pharmacologically treated, over $1 trillion of economic impact. The penetration base case for everything that followed.

Mounjaro's US launch curve against Trulicity and semaglutide, plus the realized-price mechanics: 73% access across commercial and Part D lives at July 2023, paid prescriptions up to 67%, and the non-covered $25 copay card ending June 30.

How the oncology pipeline was rebuilt by acquisition: Loxo (Feb 2019) through mutant-selective PI3K-alpha, Biclonics bispecifics, camptothecin and early-stage ADCs, the POINT radioligand portfolio and manufacturing (Oct 2023) to miniprotein radiopharmaceuticals (May 2024).
December 2024: Lilly still behind Novo Nordisk in US incretin prescriptions, 48.7% versus 50.7%, in a market growing 45% year-on-year. The last quarter before the crossover.

Management's addressable-market arithmetic: 8 million US incretin prescriptions in April 2025 against 170M+ patients projected for 2030, i.e. 5% penetration, plus a ~1 billion ex-US population. The denominator is prevalence, not payer-covered lives.

Why the oral changes the physical constraint: orforglipron runs on a separate small-molecule manufacturing footprint with no cold-chain requirement, with at-risk investment ahead of launch. The escape from the peptide fill-finish bottleneck.
The only quantified incretin supply metric Lilly has published: saleable doses produced in 1H 2025 were 1.6x 1H 2024. The capacity ramp that ended the shortage, sized.

The formulary exclusion showing up first in new patients: Zepbound US branded anti-obesity TRx share rose 5pp to 66% while NBRx share declined 6pp to 68%, attributed to loss of access on CVS template plans effective 7/1/25. New-patient share leads total share.
The crossover quarter: Lilly at 57.0% of US incretin prescriptions versus Novo at 42.5%, in a market still growing 41% year-on-year.

Management's own statement that the binding constraint moved: from single marketed product, demand outpacing supply and payer barriers, to a broad portfolio, 13 sites under construction, and access models built around LillyDirect. Supply is solved; access and price are the problem.

The $55bn manufacturing programme and its 13 sites, split between the API-and-Dry network (Lebanon IN x2, Huntsville, Puerto Rico, Houston, Katwijk, Limerick, Goochland) and the Parenteral-and-Devices network (RTP, Concord, Kenosha, Alzey). The dollar figure appears nowhere in the 10-K.

The answer to single-molecule concentration: 75%+ of new clinical medicines sit outside incretins and amylins, mapped to US patient populations - chronic pain 51M, elevated Lp(a) 63M, preclinical Alzheimer's 20M, early breast cancer 3M.

The R&D productivity claim restated on a shifted window - 24 NME launches from 2015-2025, versus the 2021 deck's 20-in-10 for 2014-2023 - plus 3.5 years faster than industry from discovery to first launch, and 39 business-development transactions in 2025.

The infrastructure built around the molecule: LillyDirect served 1 million+ patients in 2025, Lilly Catalyze 360 has supported 180+ biotechs since 2023, and the NVIDIA collaboration is building the industry's most powerful supercomputer. The only public sizing of LillyDirect.

The price/volume/FX decomposition by geography: FY2025 revenue $65,179M on +50% volume and (6)% price, with US price at (10)%. The single most important table for understanding how this business grows.
US incretin share at 60.5%, up 2.6pp on the quarter, but market growth decelerating to +33% year-on-year from +45% a year earlier.

FY2025 capital allocation: $10.9bn after-tax R&D, $7.8bn capital investments, $4.1bn business development, $5.4bn dividend, $4.1bn buyback. Business development is now 0.53x capex, against 2.5x in 2017-2021.

The 2026 guidance bridge, and the four named causes of a low-to-mid-teens global price decline: the US government access agreement, Zepbound direct-to-patient pricing, Mounjaro reimbursement in China, and Medicaid MFN pricing. Three of the four are permanent.
The first sequential decline in the series: US incretin share 60.1%, down from 60.5%, with market growth down to +30% year-on-year. The US share gain has plateaued.

Where the growth moved: the international incretin market grew 77% year-on-year in early 2026 with Lilly at 53.2% versus Novo at 46.8% - a 6pp lead abroad against a 21pp lead at home, in lower-priced markets.

Foundayo launch mechanics: retail from April 9, 12+ telehealth platforms at ~35% of launch volume, access at 2 of 3 major PBMs, and management's testable claim that 80%+ of prescriptions are new incretin patients rather than switches.

Retatrutide TRIUMPH-1: 65% of participants on 12mg reached BMI below 30 and 33% reached BMI below 25 - weight loss at levels previously associated with bariatric surgery. The next molecule competing with Lilly's own tirzepatide.

Eloralintide, the non-incretin option: 12.4% weight loss at 3mg with no titration and placebo-like tolerability (nausea 13% versus 14% on placebo), 16.4% at the highest dose with no plateau. Tolerability as a distinct competitive axis.

The segmentation thesis in one slide: the portfolio mapped onto seven patient needs - greater weight loss, tolerability, minimal titration, ultra-long acting, lean-mass benefit, metabolic benefit, injection frequency - plus oral dual/triple agonists and adjacencies.
